subject: physics
question_text: Show that steel is more elastic than rubber.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Very Short Answer Question 12 (printed p.99). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Y = stress/strain; for equal stress, the material with the smaller strain has the larger Y; steel's Young's modulus (about 2 × 10¹¹ N/m²) is roughly four orders of magnitude above rubber's, which is the standard NCERT comparison.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Compare the extensions
lines: Take a steel wire and a rubber wire
of the same length and area. Apply
the same stretching force to each.
The rubber wire extends far more
steps.why: Comparing the extension for the same force and the same dimensions is comparing the strain for the same stress — exactly the ratio that Young's modulus measures.
common_mistakes: Comparing wires of different length or area. The comparison only works when the force, length and area are the same for both.
Describing the extensions without saying the force applied is the same for both wires.
steps.memory_tip: Same force, same size, different stretch: that stretch is the strain to compare.
steps.margin_note: Marked for stating equal force and equal dimensions, then the larger extension in rubber.

steps.label: The conclusion
lines: Since Y = stress / strain, the larger
strain in rubber for the same stress

lines.text: Steel is more elastic than rubber

steps.why: A material is called more elastic when it deforms less for the same stress and returns fully to its original shape; a larger Young's modulus means less strain for the same stress, so a higher Y is the sign of the more elastic material.
common_mistakes: Calling rubber more elastic because it stretches more. Elastic means less deformation for the same stress, so a bigger stretch means LESS elastic, not more.
Confusing elastic with flexible. Rubber is more flexible, but steel is more elastic.
steps.memory_tip: Elastic means it barely moves and springs back — the small-strain material wins, so steel beats rubber.
steps.margin_note: Marked for naming Y(steel) greater than Y(rubber) and stating that the larger Y is the more elastic material.

insider_note: The mark is lost by calling rubber 'more elastic' because it stretches more — elastic means less deformation for the same stress, not more.
